title: vvvvvv
text: VVVVVV is an old-school-charmer built on two simple principles: you can invert gravity, and if you touch a spike you die. Sounds simple enough! It's that simple premise that makes the game so easy to pick up, and also so easy to wedge a pickax through your keyboard. Fans of VERY old-school games will probably enjoy this most of all. It's surprisingly longer than you'd expect (took me 2 hours to complete, in short 25-minute bursts, with full grief counseling sessions in between), and the music is absolutely ROCKING. Definitely recommended when on sale (I picked it up for 50 cents, an absolute steal). When you beat it, wear it like a badge of honor, just like you did when you beat Battletoads on the NES.

title: wakfu
text: I loved Final Fantasy Tactics A2 and the Pokemon Mystery Dungeon series and always wished for a multiplayer version of those games. This game does a pretty good job of putting the combat experiences of those games in a multiplayer setting. Besides the combat, I also enjoyed the game's environmental mechanics because it kind of gives me a Harvest Moon or Animal Crossing kind of vibe where the world gives you these resources to do things with, and the players are responsible for tending to them or making something out of them. As for the grinding, I personally don't know if it is actually necessary or not, but in any case I managed to skip the first story quests altogether and head to my chosen nation (Bonta) and then proceeded to grind the highest level mobs and dungeons that I could manage, purely because I love overwhelming myself in these tactics games and barely pulling through. It also helps that the only punishment for death is no exp gain for a lost battle, reduced stats for about 3 minutes and a respawn back to the previous checkpoint area of your choosing. I've spent no money on the game so far, but I might in the future if I keep playing. Paying players get some nice bonuses, but I've been playing comfortably without them. There's also some nifty costumes and stuff too. I recommend the game because it's free and I enjoy it. If you get it, I'd definitely recommend doing the tutorial and trying out a few different classes. I went through a couple classes and then went with the Elitrope as my main because I personally loved the portal mechanic. My brother went with the archer because he loved the obscene range and then the huppermage because of the elemental/light attack dynamic. There's a lot of variety, so don't be afraid to try a few out. Also, your lower level alts will gain an experience multiplier to make grinding levels faster,

title: wargame: airland battle
text: ***Edit: According to experts, the game is in fact pausible. I am a fool and a monster. Please down-vote my heretical review. It is offensive propaganda.*** Short version: Great for people who love wargames that can (and want to) keep up with the blinding speed. Not so great for everyone else. *** I’ve tried so hard to like this game. I really like the idea of the game, but after three separate goes of it, I give up. Despite the old-school vibe of awesome military minutia and an interesting and believable historical setting, the gameplay is closer to Starcraft than it is to Close Combat. The game looks and feels like it should have deep tactical gameplay, and frankly it probably does if you can keep up with the constant micromanagement demands of moving, supplying, mounting/dismounting troops, calling in airstrikes and watching every corner of your line while also purchasing and placing reinforcements for your losses. Before I played, I assume this was a slower and higher-echelon game in the Company of Heroes mold. Nope. Higher echelon yes, but the speed makes Company of Heroes look like Steel Panthers. Don’t get me wrong, I don’t think this is a bad game. For a small subset of gamers who love military minutia and breakneck RTS pace, I’m sure it’s heaven. Everyone else is either going to be overwhelmed by the detail or the speed. For me, it’s the latter. I love all the detail. I just wish everything didn’t move so fast that I couldn’t possibly keep up with it. If the game had a “pause for orders” option, or maybe even a speed setting, I suspect I’d really enjoy it. As it stands, the game is simply overwhelming, and I think I’ve just uninstalled it for good. If you love nitty-gritty, realistic military sims and have an ample supply of amphetamines to keep up with all the clicking, this game is absolutely worth your time. If not, I’d pass.

title: wargame: airland battle
text: Let me start this review by saying that I REALLY want to recommend this game. Really. As far as RTS games go, this Wargame Airland Battle has done a lot of things very right, and I’ll start by talking about these. Firstly the ability to zoom from the full scope of the map right down to see individual men running across a field really gives you a great perspective. You sit with your 12 tanks, 8 armoured personnel carriers, 4 mobile AA units, 4 tank destroyers, 40 mixed AA/AT infantry and recon team and think 'yeah, this is a nice army.' you set them up in nice defensive positions to await the rush of enemy units, maybe you even set down some artillery to cover them. Then you zoom out to see where the enemy is at and notice how rapidly the map swallows your 'nice' army until you can barely see them; little coloured specks in an otherwise insignificant woodland in a corner of the battlefield. It’s really absolutely brilliant and I love it. Another great feature is the persistent units; units you lose in one battle stay lost for the next. If your super powerful expensive helo gets shot down, you can’t call him in again, which gives you a real attachment to your units and makes you think twice before sending your recon and choppers on what’s probably a suicide run. I also love the unit resupply mechanics, all units have ammo and fuel which need to be maintained. leaving an AA squad out in some far flung corner of the map just to be a♥♥♥♥♥♥to your opponent only works until they’ve used their 8 missiles, after that they really are useless until you can resupply them. the resupply mechanic hasn’t been overthought though, all units can repair, collect fuel and any kind of ammo just by being in the resupply radius of a unit or building, there’s no micromanaging the carrying of 8000 different kinds of ammunition to the front lines *ahem* Men Of War *ahem*. Sadly this brings us to the negative points. Campaigns consist of a Risk board game style army movement that feels unnecessary with powers such as nukes and reinforcements that leave little impact on the actual 'board'. I was told by one mission to nuke an enemy sector before attacking it, I braced myself for the horror of what I was about to do. I was told it would be done within 24 hours (1 turn) of my order, so I gave the order and waited. And waited. And waited. Did it happen? Is it on route? If I attack now will I nuke my own men in a minute? No indication was given whatsoever that this horrific deed had been done, and it’s in touches like this that Wargame falls down. When playing a battle you are given no obvious objective, no indication of what to do, just to deploy your units here. Then the battle happens, you kill some stuff and suddenly, without any warning, the battle screen disappears and you’re told you won a major victory. Did I? I don’t feel like I did. I had no idea what I was supposed to be doing. It seems the battles consist of just killing the enemy units faster than they kill yours, until you've killed enough that the battle ends. Whilst this is fine (ish) for multiplayer, from a solo or co-op campaign, I really want more. Just little touches like being told to hold a sector whilst VIPs evacuate or to secure a supply route, just something. it even boils down to the same main objective - hold here whilst the enemy throws units at you, but the simple addition of some kind of objective makes the whole experience more tangible and less just like a punching match. Lastly the units, whilst very varied, are gone into in far too much detail. You’re told exactly which weapon each unit uses, whether that’s a strela-2 or RPG-7, AK, RPK, or a bajillion others that I can't name off the top of my head, it’s not necessary. I wouldn’t mind though if the game told you what kind of vehicle/squad it is, but instead you're told that it has a KONKURS, and that it has 2 AP power and 6 HE power (totally making that up, but you get the idea), the game neglects to tell you however whether this is an anti-tank launcher, an anti-air launcher, some kind of unguided rocket, a recoilless rifle, etc. etc. you can make guesses by its rate of fire and total ammo count, but I’ve been surprised on more than one occasion, and I would say I have a fair knowledge of modern firearms. Basically it gets very anal about the units you have available, but fails to tell you how good they are against other unit types. All in all then I really can't recommend this game, it provides a great platform for strategy gaming, but give you no direction or variation in your attempts to do so. The game is also impossibly difficult at times, totally without warning. Here’s my overall rating then - + Lovely graphics + Some great mechanics + Wide unit variety - No direction given to player - Some not so great mechanics - No mission variety - Sporadic difficulty jumps 6/10 There’s better RTS games on the market, maybe Red Dragon improves upon these points.
